nodes.label: InfraGrid Application
nodes.description: The We.PLM Azure Infrastructure Register app, branded InfraGrid, tracking resources, environments, and subscriptions in one place.

nodes.label: index.html Entry Point
nodes.description: Vite SPA entry point that mounts the React root div and loads /src/main.tsx as a module script.

nodes.label: Open Graph Single Preview Strategy
nodes.description: index.html ships one static OG/Twitter preview for the whole app rather than per-route.
nodes.rationale: A plain SPA's index.html is all a sharing-card crawler (WhatsApp, Teams, Slack, etc.) ever reads, since none of them execute JS, so per-route previews are not achievable.

nodes.label: Scope Discipline
nodes.description: Agents must stay within the requested task's scope: no unrelated features, refactors, dependency upgrades, or schema changes without explicit approval.
nodes.rationale: The objective is to implement the requested change while preserving existing functionality and architecture.

nodes.label: Minimal-Change Rule
nodes.description: Change only what the task requires; no unrelated refactors, renames, moves, or opportunistic cleanup until explicitly instructed otherwise.
nodes.rationale: If a required change exposes an architectural problem outside the task, report it rather than silently expanding the scope.

nodes.label: File Modification Rules
nodes.description: Files may only be renamed, moved, or deleted when the task explicitly requires it, with all references updated and the project reverified.

nodes.label: Dependency Introduction Rules
nodes.description: No new NuGet package, version upgrade, or external service dependency without explicit approval.

nodes.label: Asynchronous Method Suffix Rule
nodes.description: Async methods must use the full `Asynchronous` suffix (e.g. GetUserAsynchronous), never the abbreviated `Async`.

nodes.label: Asynchronous Programming Rules
nodes.description: I/O-bound work must be async, never `.Result`/`.Wait()` or `Task.Run()` as a substitute, and CancellationToken must propagate.

nodes.label: JSON Property PascalCase Rule
nodes.description: All API JSON property names, and the C# response model properties producing them, must use PascalCase, enforced app-wide in serialization config.

nodes.label: Feature Models Rule
nodes.description: All feature-specific enums/structs/interfaces/records/classes/DTOs live under Features/${FeatureName}/Models/, while behavioral classes stay in their architectural folders.

nodes.label: Global Helpers Singleton Pattern
nodes.description: All global helper classes follow a sealed class plus private static readonly `_current`/public `Current` singleton pattern.

nodes.label: Zero-Mock Data / Pure Data Grounding Rule
nodes.description: All rendered data must come from live backend API responses; hardcoded mock fallback arrays are forbidden in production controllers.
nodes.norm_label: zero-mock data / pure data grounding rule

nodes.label: Database Rules
nodes.description: Async-only DB operations, no manual DbContext instantiation or Singleton registration, parameterized queries, and every table named via entity.ToTable using the IG_{Name}TBL template.

nodes.label: TanStack Query Hub Pattern
nodes.description: Centralized singleton TanstackQueryClientService hub exposes all query/mutation hooks per feature for uniform caching and invalidation.

nodes.label: Global Components Structure
nodes.description: Code used across multiple features, or explicitly app-wide, moves to global Service/Constants/Models/Utilities/Middlewares/Helpers/Exceptions/Validators folders.

nodes.label: DTO and Entity Separation
nodes.description: Controllers accept/return DTOs only; persistence entities are never exposed through API endpoints, with mapping occurring outside the controller.

nodes.label: Controller Rules
nodes.description: Controllers call the feature service, validate via Assertion, return `APIResponse<T>`, use try-catch, and never contain business logic or touch persistence entities directly.

nodes.label: Component Hierarchy & Controller Roles
nodes.description: Defines the four controller tiers: Screen Controllers, Modal Controllers, Screen Routes, and Shared Components.

nodes.label: Dependency Injection Rules
nodes.description: Dependencies must be constructor-injected; controllers/services must not manually `new` other application services.

nodes.label: Feature Architecture
nodes.description: Each business feature gets a standardized Features/${FeatureName}/ folder with its own Controller, Services, Assertion, Constants, Models, Utilities.

nodes.label: One-Definition-Per-File Model Invariant
nodes.description: Each enum/interface/type alias in src/Models/ gets its own file (*EnumModel.ts/*InterfaceModel.ts/*TypeModel.ts), exported both named and default.

nodes.label: Explicit Component Signatures & JSX Return Types
nodes.description: Every React functional component needs an exported `[Name]Props` interface and an explicit `React.JSX.Element` return type.
nodes.norm_label: explicit component signatures & jsx return types

nodes.label: API Endpoint Naming Rules
nodes.description: Every endpoint must start with `/Api/V1` and use complete PascalCase segments, never abbreviations, kebab-case, snake_case, or camelCase.

nodes.label: Assertion Pattern
nodes.description: Every feature needing request validation has a Singleton Features/${FeatureName}/Assertion/${FeatureName}Assertion.cs class that controllers call instead of duplicating null checks.

nodes.label: Isolated Global Type Files (src/Types/*Type.ts)
nodes.description: Every global data model lives in its own *Type.ts file, re-exported through a central src/Types/index.ts barrel; monolithic types.ts is forbidden.

nodes.label: Code Quality & Pre-Generation Checklist
nodes.description: Final checklist (typed components, CON-sourced constants, singleton services, 0 tsc/build errors) gating any client code change.

nodes.label: ApplicationNetworkAPIConfiguration
nodes.description: Frontend network endpoint configuration file under src/Configurations/ that targets the backend API's route contract.

nodes.label: Zustand Reactive State Stores (*Store.ts)
nodes.description: Global client-only reactive state (auth session, permissions, ephemeral UI config) is managed via Zustand stores in src/Store/.

nodes.label: Modal Bi-directional Exit Physics
nodes.description: Header/X and top-backdrop clicks exit 'down'; footer Cancel/Close/Submit and deep-backdrop clicks exit 'up'.

nodes.label: Exception Handling & Status Code Mapping
nodes.description: Known exceptions map to specific HTTP status codes (Validation to 400, Unauthorized to 401, etc.); unexpected exceptions never leak `ex.Message` to clients.

nodes.label: Structured Logging Rules
nodes.description: Logging must use structured message templates, never string interpolation, and must never log passwords, tokens, API keys, or connection strings.

nodes.label: Modal Data Caching Ref Pattern
nodes.description: Modals cache the last-seen entity in a ref so content doesn't vanish mid-exit-animation when the prop becomes null.

nodes.label: Backend Security Rules
nodes.description: Never hardcode or log secrets, never return raw exception details, never disable TLS validation, and never trust client-provided identity/role claims.

nodes.label: Testing Rules
nodes.description: New business logic needs tests following the existing test architecture; tests must verify behavior, not just increase coverage.

nodes.label: Case Conventions
nodes.description: PascalCase for files/components/types, camelCase for functions/variables, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constant values and storage keys.

nodes.label: Type-Specific Naming Suffixes
nodes.description: PascalCase types/classes must carry an architectural suffix (Controller, Service, Assertion, Middleware, DTO, Record, Type, CON, Utility, Helper, Validator, Exception).

nodes.label: Client Directory Topology
nodes.description: Prescribed src/ folder hierarchy: Configurations, Constants, Features, Models, Routes, Router, Services, Shared, Store, Types, Utilities.

nodes.label: Fields & Parameters Naming
nodes.description: Private fields use _camelCase, parameters and locals use camelCase, properties use PascalCase.

nodes.label: Strong Typing Policy
nodes.description: Prohibits `dynamic`/untyped `object` and `var` where an explicit type is possible; code must compile without nullable-reference warnings.

nodes.label: Frontend Abbreviations Policy
nodes.description: Prohibits abbreviations in code identifiers except an explicit full-caps allow-list: EN, IP, DNS, URL, SMTP, OS, VM, DBA, SLA, CET, SXI.

nodes.label: Route Factory Pattern
nodes.description: Route strings must never be hardcoded in controllers; all routes are declared as PascalCase constants in Factories/ApplicationRouteFactory.cs.

nodes.label: Backend Abbreviations Policy
nodes.description: Same full-word-over-abbreviation rule as the frontend, allow-listing EN, IP, DNS, URL, SMTP, OS, VM, DBA, SLA, CET, SXI plus CPU, RAM, GB.

nodes.label: Class-Based Singleton Service Architecture
nodes.description: Services, helpers, and utilities (except React components and Zustand hooks) must be classes exposing a public static `current` singleton instance.

nodes.label: Backend Singleton Rules
nodes.description: Singletons must be stateless and safe app-wide, never hold request- or user-specific mutable state; DbContext and Controllers must never be Singleton.

nodes.label: MSC (Model-Service-Controller) Architecture
nodes.description: Strict layered frontend architecture (Router to Controller to Service to Model/Type, plus Shared Components) enforced across the React 19 + TypeScript client.

nodes.label: Zero `any` Invariant
nodes.description: Strictly prohibits `any` throughout the client codebase in favor of exact interfaces, unions, generics, or narrowed `unknown`.

nodes.label: Strict File & Symbol Naming Invariants
nodes.description: Table mapping each architectural role (ScreenController, ModalController, ScreenRoute, SharedComponent, CON, Service, Utility, Helper, EnumModel, InterfaceModel, TypeModel, Store) to a required file/export suffix.

nodes.label: Build and Verification Rules
nodes.description: The agent must never claim build/test success without actually performing verification, and must explicitly state when verification was not performed.
nodes.rationale: Never imply successful verification based solely on code inspection.

nodes.label: APIResponse Naming & Structure Rules
nodes.description: The response wrapper must be named exactly `APIResponse`/`APIResponse<T>`, never `ApiResponse` variants, with consistent success/error structure and no internal detail leakage.

nodes.label: Utility vs Helper Distinction
nodes.description: Utilities are app-wide singleton logic usable by any feature; Helpers are feature-specific singleton logic scoped to one feature's own domain data.

nodes.label: Validators Pattern
nodes.description: Validators are Singletons exposing a single public `bool Validate(...)` method performing exactly one type of validation.

nodes.label: Constant & Configuration Classes (*CON.ts)
nodes.description: Zero magic strings or inline static arrays; all constants live as `public static readonly` ALL_CAPS properties on *CON.ts classes.

nodes.label: AI Agent Repository Inspection Rules
nodes.description: Before coding, the agent must inspect the relevant feature directory, existing implementations, DI registrations, and routes, then make the smallest necessary change.

nodes.label: Rule Precedence
nodes.description: Conflict resolution order within this file: explicit task requirements, then security/correctness, existing architecture/contracts, feature rules, global rules, style.
nodes.rationale: Per this repo's root CLAUDE.md, conflicts and ambiguity between the two CODING-RULES.md files, or between either file and anything else, are resolved by asking the user — which explicitly overrides this section's own precedence ordering.

nodes.label: Agent Assumption Policy
nodes.description: Only trivial assumptions not affecting architecture, behavior, security, contracts, data integrity, or dependencies are allowed; material assumptions require asking first.
nodes.rationale: Per this repo's root CLAUDE.md, this policy's tolerance for trivial assumptions does not get to resolve anything on its own in this repo; the user decides every time a conflict or ambiguity arises.

nodes.label: Reuse Component Before Writing New Code Rule
nodes.description: Requires checking for an existing reusable component before writing new UI code; genuinely new code must be a proper SharedComponent, never inline JSX.
nodes.norm_label: reuse component before writing new code rule

nodes.label: No-Hallucination Rules
nodes.description: The agent must never invent classes, methods, endpoints, packages, or other project facts; missing information must be asked about, not guessed.
nodes.rationale: A plausible assumption must never be presented as an established project fact.

nodes.label: Existing Code Is the Source of Truth
nodes.description: The existing repository architecture and implementation is treated as the primary source of truth over personal preference.
nodes.norm_label: existing code is the source of truth
nodes.rationale: Preserve existing behavior unless the task explicitly requires behavior changes; do not rewrite functioning code merely to match personal preferences.

nodes.label: Ask When Pattern Not Covered Rule
nodes.description: Workflow rule instructing agents to ask the user rather than guess when a coding pattern isn't explicitly covered by the spec.
nodes.norm_label: ask when pattern not covered rule
nodes.rationale: This file will not have an explicit rule for every situation, so the gap should be surfaced rather than picked silently.

nodes.label: Research Before Writing Code Rule
nodes.description: Workflow rule requiring agents to check sibling AssetSphere/SignForge implementations before writing new client code.
nodes.rationale: This project's patterns are meant to replicate what AssetSphere and SignForge already ship, not invent something new.
